solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Avant-garde Somalian painting — not 19

indicators.note: avant-garde art breaks with convention, so the letters of the word Somalian are rearranged experimentally

explanation.surface: A daring piece of art from Somalia is up for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 19, MODERN ART: the painting meant is a famous old one, not a modern work.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait is the best-known Renaissance painting, an Old Master rather than a modern work.

clue.text: Note on 'Denominazione di Origine Controllata' red wine

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so the note comes first

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale
DOC is the abbreviation for the Italian wine quality label

explanation.surface: A label note on an Italian-certified bottle of red.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a district of Bordeaux whose name is used for its red claret.

clue.text: Keep flying for ever in Pan's domain

definitions.meaning: to keep flying for ever is never to touch down on the ground
the island where Peter Pan lives in J M Barrie's story

explanation.surface: Peter Pan flies on endlessly over his own kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into two words: if you keep flying for ever, you 'never land'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan's realm in Barrie's play is the island where children never grow up.

clue.text: Girl concealing rubbish about the German that's heard in 11

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the other pieces hidden within it

parts.note: lass is a girl

indicators.note: about signals turning the word for rubbish round

parts.note: rot means rubbish, nonsense
der is the German masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A girl hides some German nonsense that gets spoken in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is PUBLIC BAR, where the landlord calls time; 'that's heard in' points to the call being shouted, not a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlord's call for final drinks before closing time is shouted across a pub's public bar.

clue.text: Gullible person getting direct attention over blood poisoning

parts.note: a sap is a fool, someone easily taken in

indicators.note: in a down clue, over signals that the pair of words is read upwards

parts.note: to aim is to direct
ear means attention, as in 'give me your ear'

explanation.surface: A fool needs urgent care because of septicaemia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses AIM EAR to give RAEMIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapraemia is a medical term for septic toxins from decaying matter circulating in the bloodstream.

clue.text: Supporter with Russian car in World cup venue

parts.note: a bra supports, a crossword favourite
ZiL was a Russian maker of cars and limousines

explanation.surface: A fan arrives by Russian car at the football tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a football fan; it is underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazil hosted football's 2014 World Cup, which was weeks away when this puzzle appeared.

clue.text: Means of transport supplier of pork pies set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written going upwards

parts.note: pork pies is rhyming slang for lies, so the one who supplies them is a liar

explanation.surface: A van delivering pork pies gets put in place.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang is Cockney wordplay: 'pork pies' rhymes with 'lies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Railways carry passengers and freight, so travelling by train is one way of getting about.

clue.text: Initially Eddie Izzard turns up with ladies' underwear item that's stripy

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the two letters are read upwards
initially picks the first letter of the comedian's first name

parts.note: izzard is an old name for the letter Z
a bra is an item of ladies' underwear

explanation.surface: The comedian Eddie Izzard, known for cross-dressing, appears in a striped bra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Izzard' is no surname here: it is an old word for the letter Z. 'turns up' makes EZ into ZE.
explanation.definitionFit: The African horse-like animal is known for its black and white striped coat.

clue.text: My word, Brydon's upset with character often mentioned in 'The Trip to Italy'

definitions.text: character often mentioned in 'The Trip to Italy'

parts.note: lor is a dialect exclamation of surprise, like 'my word'

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the name are put in disorder

parts.note: the comedian's surname taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: Rob Brydon is annoyed by a character in his TV travel show.
explanation.walkthrough: In the series The Trip to Italy, Steve Coogan and Rob Brydon follow the trail of the Romantic poets around Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet who lived and wrote in Italy is a recurring reference point as the comedians retrace his journey.

clue.text: Touch up with an instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue, up signals that the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: the tuba is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A tuba player gives the piece some finishing touches.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that abut are adjacent, meeting along an edge.

clue.text: With unfinished strip, attempts to con the ref

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to divest is to strip

explanation.surface: A footballer in a half-removed shirt tries to fool the referee.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, a player who dives falls deliberately to win a foul or penalty.

clue.text: Not a saloon, but Capri bulb that's blown

indicators.note: a blown bulb has burst, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A Ford Capri isn't a saloon car, though its bulb has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saloon' suggests a car, helped by the Capri. In British pubs the saloon bar was the smarter room and the public bar the plainer one.
explanation.definitionFit: A British pub traditionally had two rooms, the saloon and the cheaper, more basic alternative.

clue.text: Combats Republican workers perhaps following vehicle

indicators.note: following places the other pieces after the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
GOP, the Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party
worker ants are an example of the insects, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Republican labourers fight it out behind a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combats' looks like a verb; it is short for combat trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat trousers are loose trousers with big side pockets, the same garment under another name.

clue.text: Cutting remark from the Broadcasters' Audience Research Board

definitions.meaning: the UK body that measures television audiences, known by its initials

explanation.surface: A sharp jibe comes from the TV ratings body.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is the acronym of the board's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed, wounding comment is likened to the sharp hooked point of an arrow.

clue.text: Edges aren't seen with this sort of cricket bowling

parts.note: French cricket is a simple children's game played with a bat and ball
seam is a kind of bowling in cricket, using the ball's stitching

explanation.surface: A batsman doesn't get any edges against this type of bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edges' suggests a batsman's snicks; they are raw fabric edges, hidden in this sewing technique.
explanation.definitionFit: This sewing technique encloses the raw edges of the fabric inside the stitching, so they are invisible.

clue.text: Fish around river for scrap

indicators.note: around means the fish's name goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: the shad is a fish of the herring family

explanation.surface: An angler fishes round the river for scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment of broken glass or pottery is a small piece, a scrap.

definitions.meaning: these are a few clock readings, a handful of moments

explanation.surface: A timetable lists services that run only intermittently.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the first definition is 'some times'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens on and off happens only occasionally, now and then.

clue.text: One proposes to include iron filings in song title

indicators.note: the proposer's name is made to include the other piece

parts.note: a mover is one who proposes a motion in a meeting

indicators.note: filings are bits filed off, so the metal's letters are broken up

explanation.surface: Someone suggests adding iron filings to the title of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filings' rearranges IRON into ONRI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mancini–Mercer number from Breakfast at Tiffany's is one of the best-known film songs.

clue.text: Making progress concerning first band played on Radio One

parts.note: on means about, concerning

parts.words: first band played on Radio One
parts.note: The Move's 'Flowers in the Rain' was the first record played on BBC Radio 1 in 1967

explanation.surface: A band gets ahead after the first airing on Radio One.
explanation.walkthrough: BBC Radio 1 is Britain's national pop music station.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone advancing is travelling or getting somewhere, as an idiom for progress.

clue.text: Very neat pupil's upset about zero for interview with the public

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the zero
upset knocks the letters of the schoolchild word into a new order

parts.note: the schoolchild word taken as written, the possessive adding no letter
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A very tidy pupil is upset after getting nought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very neat' looks like praise; it is V and OX. 'upset' turns PUPIL into PPULI, which goes 'about' O to make POPULI.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'voice of the people', it is the full form of vox pop, a street interview with passers-by.

clue.text: Paintings etc. not marred in reproduction

indicators.note: a reproduction is a copy made anew, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Reproductions of contemporary pictures aren't spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings and sculpture of the twentieth century make up a broad genre covering many forms.

clue.text: Apparently naked president

definitions.meaning: split as ..., it says nothing on, as if unclothed

explanation.surface: A US president is seemingly undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: NIX is slang for nothing, so 'nix on' means wearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Milhous Nixon held the American presidency from 1969 until Watergate forced him out in 1974.

clue.text: President thanks a newspaper

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A president sends his thanks to a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: William Howard Taft was the 27th US president, later Chief Justice.

clue.text: Savage time in Florida

indicators.note: in means the time is placed inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A brutal period in Florida's history.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild and untamed, like animals that have gone back to the wild.

clue.text: Condition discommoding the orators

indicators.note: discommoding means putting out, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: An ailment is bothering the public speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful inflamed pharynx is a common ailment, the sort that troubles speakers.

clue.text: Player without an Oscar getting an award

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the award goes round the letter

parts.note: OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor without an Oscar has to settle for another honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' and 'Oscar' suggest an actor; the player is a musician and Oscar is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument stands for the musician playing it, as in an orchestra's first oboe.

clue.text: Snacks made from recycled pasta

indicators.note: recycled material is remade into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Leftover pasta gets turned into nibbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Small Spanish savoury dishes are served as appetisers with drinks.

clue.text: Shot a pirate

definitions.meaning: a stroke in golf, cricket or boxing that curves or swings across
Captain ..., the villain of Peter Pan

explanation.surface: Someone guns down a buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as a verb; it is a noun, a kind of stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain James Hook is the one-handed buccaneer in Barrie's Peter Pan.

clue.text: Traveller having a brandy at work and a loo break

parts.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape skins
op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: break shatters the toilet word so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone drinks brandy on the job and takes toilet breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The thirteenth-century Venetian merchant journeyed to China and wrote about it.

clue.text: Supply an online 13

parts.note: e-, as in email, means electronic or online
13 is a cutting remark, and a quip is a witty one

explanation.surface: Post a sharp remark on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 across is BARB, here read as its sense 'cutting remark'.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone with what is needed is to provide them, to supply.

clue.text: Somehow sail around this country with a dog

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go round the country
somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are arranged in some new way

parts.note: for a British setter, this country is the UK

explanation.surface: Sailing round Britain with a dog on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' yields SALI from the sailing word; 'this country' is the UK because the setter is British.
explanation.definitionFit: The saluki is a slender Middle Eastern hunting hound, a breed of dog.

clue.text: Fabulous creatures out to disarm me

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mythical monsters are trying to take my weapons away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means of fable, not wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendary sea beings, half woman and half fish, belong to fable.
